title: CS amp, resistive load
description: Common-source stage with a physical resistor as the load. $g_m$ is fixed from the bandwidth spec (with an explicit over-design factor) and $g_m/I_D$ is the efficiency knob; the load resistor $R_{load}$ sets both the gain and the DC drop that eats output headroom. This is the classic gain-vs-headroom trade made explicit: a bigger $R_{load}$ raises the gain but drops more of the supply, so the output DC level $V_{out}$ = VDD - $I*R_{load}$ sinks toward the device's saturation floor. The device's drain sits at that level, so its $V_{DS}$ is $V_{out}$ and nothing is typed for it: with $g_m$ and $g_m/I_D$ both bound, the current is $g_m/(g_m/I_D)$, a closed form of the params, and the bind places the drain from it.

params.name: cdd_est
params.note: output-node parasitic estimate (drain + wiring); refine from extraction

params.name: gbw_margin
params.note: over-design factor on gm for parasitics and PVT

params.name: R_load
params.note: load resistor: higher R raises the gain but drops more of the supply (less headroom)

equations.name: Rout
equations.note: the resistance this stage presents at its output: the load resistor in parallel with the device output resistance. The load knob is already inside this row and inside the gain, so the loading contract here is the arithmetic rather than a separate rule

equations.name: Av
equations.note: gm into the load resistor in parallel with the device output resistance

equations.name: V_drop
equations.note: DC drop across the load resistor

equations.name: V_out
equations.note: the output DC level, which is also the device's drain-source voltage. The bind writes the same level with the current expanded as gm/gm_id, because a bind evaluates before any row

equations.name: vn_in
equations.note: device channel thermal density plus the load resistor's 4kT/R_load current noise referred to the input by 1/gm

equations.name: cgg_in
equations.note: estimate: the capacitance the input terminal presents — this stage's gate capacitance and nothing else. Gate capacitance only, because the Miller term needs the gate-drain fraction and these tables do not carry it, so a driving stage sees more than this. No rule reads it

equations.name: I_q
equations.note: estimate: quiescent supply current — the branch current, which here is an OUTPUT of the sizing rather than a setting: the bandwidth spec fixes gm, and the chosen inversion divides it down to a current. The datasheet line for comparing designs; no rule reads it

checks.note: gm/ID cannot exceed the weak-inversion ceiling of the data
read from the table's own noise where it carries it, and from the γ = 1 estimate otherwise; the simulator owns noise sign-off
actual GBW into CL plus the parasitic estimate; the over-design factor should keep this green
